title: Lipscomb's strict training: Arban, tone, reading
summary: Lipscomb was a terrific trumpeter who taught breathing and reading from the Arban book, ignoring Cootie's jazz on the side.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, what kind of a music book did he
have you on?
(Arban)
He had me on the album. I think that was -- yeah, album.
Oh, yeah. Right. And so you were doing exercises out of that.
Yeah.
Was he -- could he move around on the horn himself?
Oh, yeah. He was a terrific trumpeter.
He was?
Yeah.
He really was?
Uh-huh.
Oh. Strong?
Yeah.
And a good tone?
Yeah.
Oh. Well, you were fortunate weren't you?
Oh, yeah.
And he had a good embouchure.
Yeah.
So you didn't have any embouchure trouble right from the start then?
No.
I mean, he didn't have to tell you anything about blowing. You just -- it came naturally, how to blow.
Yeah. It came naturally how to blow.
He taught you about breathing.
Yeah. He taught me about breathing.
Well. You studied with him about eight years, didn't you?
I studied with him for quite a while.
Well, so what, would he work you through that book --
Yeah.
-- and take you onto the next book, and so on?
Yeah.
But all that time, he was determined you wouldn't play jazz?
That's right.
Did he think you didn't? Did he think you were doing what you were told?
(Laughter)
Or did he not care to think about it?
Well, just as long as I came in with those lessons.
Yeah. He didn't --
He didn't bother about what I was doing.
Yeah.
In the beginning, I started to messing up. Then he straightened me out.
Yeah. But once he had you doing his work --
Yeah.
Yeah. Well, Cootie, so it was in this working out these exercises and everything all the time, that you began to really develop the habit of reading, then.
Oh, yeah.
So, I mean, that just all came as a part of blowing. The reading was another part of blowing.
Yeah.
Which it wasn't in a lot of people's cases, was it? You know, a lot of people found out how to blow one way or another, and they weren't actually reading at the same time, were they?
That's right.
I mean, a lot of people didn't work from books at all, did they?
